summary: In a major national security announcement, U.S. Air Force and Space Force leadership revealed that the United States has deployed operational space control weapons on orbit. In commercial launch operations, SpaceX achieved a major milestone by completing its 700th Falcon mission, successfully carrying three telecommunications satellites into orbit. On the civil and international front, NASA welcomed Djibouti as the newest signatory to the Artemis Accords, while the agency also solicited new crop and health research proposals to advance future human exploration missions. The commercial sector demonstrated strong financial momentum, marked by Open Cosmos securing a €300 million funding round and Sophia Space setting terms with SLI for a $300 million satellite leasing agreement. In space science, astronomers using the James Webb Space Telescope and the Hubble Space Telescope discovered 27 new objects orbiting the sun far beyond Neptune, while separate Webb observations revealed that the ring system surrounding the small body Chariklo is changing over time. Additionally, solar physicists reported that the 2024 solar superstorm drained Earth's radiation belt. For upcoming space activity, viewers can watch the live broadcast tonight as two European Earth-observing satellites launch into orbit from South America.
